title: A running subagent can be moved to the background, by hand or when a message waits behind it
body:
A foreground subagent is one long tool call. Claude Code hands a queued prompt to the model only with the next tool result, so a message sent during a foreground subagent waits until the subagent returns, which can be many minutes. ACP has no request that moves a running tool call to the background, and the Claude adapter v0.101.0 exposes none among its extension methods (`_session/steering`, `_session/async_task/stop`, `_session/rename` and others). The Claude Code SDK inside the adapter can do it: its query has `backgroundTasks(tool_use_id)`, which sends a `background_tasks` control request. The adapter never calls it.

## Proposal

Once the adapter exposes it, as an extension method that takes a tool call id:

- A key, or a click on a running subagent's row, moves that subagent to the background.
- When a prompt is queued and the only thing holding the main agent is a foreground subagent, coax moves it to the background, so the prompt reaches Claude at once. The subagent keeps running and shows in the working line's agent count.

## Open

- Whether to ask the adapter's maintainers (`agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`) for the method, or to run a patched build. A request is Jack's to send. A patched build is a fork to keep current.
- Whether moving a subagent without asking each time surprises the person.
